data.commemorated_topic: (en) 50th anniversary of the New Sanctuary of Meritxell
data.comments:
(en)

The Sanctuary of Our Lady of Meritxell is a basilica located in the village of Meritxell, in the Andorran parish of Canillo. It is a place of devotion to the Virgin of Meritxell, the patron saint of the Principality of Andorra.

The original sanctuary was Romanesque in style and underwent a complete renovation in the 17th century. In 1972, the sanctuary caught fire and was completely destroyed. The fire also claimed the Romanesque carving of the Virgin—the oldest in the Principality—which had been venerated there until that time. 

The Spanish architect Ricardo Bofill Levi (Barcelona, ​​December 5, 1939–Barcelona, ​​January 14, 2022) was commissioned to design a new sanctuary. The structure features a blend of styles and is intended to harmonize with the surrounding landscape. The new building was inaugurated in 1976. Inside, a replica of the Romanesque carving of the Virgin—which was lost in the fire—continues to be venerated.

On May 13, 2014, Pope Francis designated the sanctuary a Minor Basilica. This date marked exactly one hundred years since the Virgin of Meritxell was officially declared the principal patron saint of the Valleys of Andorra by the Holy See, during the pontificate of Saint Pius X.
